description:
Canonical cross-repo truth table for the ':ack<N>' message-classification predicate. v2 collapses v1's two semantic tiers (is_ack_strict vs contains_ack_marker) into ONE strict tier: a message is an ack marker iff it contains case-sensitive ':ack' immediately followed by an ASCII digit [0-9]. Rationale: MeshCom firmware emits acks as '%-9.9s:ack%03i' (lowercase, exactly 3 ASCII digits -- lora_functions.cpp, documented in mc-chat chat.py), and a 2026-07-27 audit of both production DBs found 41 ack rows, 100% strict-format, zero case variants, zero Unicode digits, zero bare ':ack'. The v1 tier split existed only to document implementation drift, now resolved: MCProxy query.py's SQL moved from case-insensitive LIKE '%:ack%' to case-sensitive GLOB '*:ack[0-9]*' (a human message containing ':ACK99' no longer silently vanishes from history sync), both backends' Python regexes moved from \d (Unicode Nd) to [0-9] (ASCII), and webapp messageProcessor.ts's gate moved from bare .includes(':ack') to the digit-anchored isAckMessage. Every implementation now replays the SAME is_ack column; there are no runtime_overrides because the strict semantics is engine-independent by construction (JS \d is ASCII-only, Python [0-9] is ASCII-only, SQLite GLOB [0-9] is ASCII-only and case-sensitive).

ack_number is a STRING, not a number -- ':ack042' must extract '042' with the leading zero preserved (matches mc-chat decoder.py's DecodedText.ack_id contract, see TestStructuredDecode.test_decoded_text_ack_response in tests/test_decoder.py). null whenever is_ack is false. webapp's isAckMessage is boolean-only and does not extract a number; the backends' ':ack([0-9]+)' capture group defines this column.

One deliberate width difference SURVIVES v2, in push only: the push eligibility noise predicate (MCProxy push_delivery.py / mc-chat push.py / webapp pushFilter.ts) keeps the broad ':ack' substring test because it is push_contract.json-governed. Residual effect: a bare ':ack' with no digit is push-silent but history-visible. That predicate is tested by the push suites against push_contract.json, not by this fixture.

semantics.is_ack: Strict tier, the only tier in v2. True iff the text contains the case-sensitive literal ':ack' immediately followed by at least one ASCII digit [0-9] -- no separator, no uppercase, no Unicode digits. Implementations: webapp isAckMessage (src/stores/messages/predicates.ts, /:ack\d/ -- JS \d is ASCII-only, so it equals [0-9]) gating messageProcessor.ts's ack consumption; mc-chat decoder.py's re.search(r':ack([0-9]+)', message); MCProxy ingest.py's re.search(r':ack([0-9]+)', msg); MCProxy query.py's SQL pair msg GLOB '*:ack[0-9]*' (acks query) / msg NOT GLOB '*:ack[0-9]*' (every message/history query) -- exact complements, so messages and acks partition cleanly.
semantics.ack_number: String captured by the digit-anchored regex ':ack([0-9]+)' at the first match (leading zeros preserved, first marker wins). null whenever is_ack is false.

vectors.name: real_production_ack
vectors.note: Real production row shape: firmware '%-9.9s:ack%03i' -- callsign left-justified to 9 chars, then ':ack' + exactly 3 ASCII digits.

vectors.name: bare_no_digit
vectors.note: No digit after ':ack' -> not an ack. Under v1 the SQL tier excluded this from history; v2 keeps it visible as an ordinary message. It remains push-silent (the push noise predicate is deliberately broader -- see description).

vectors.name: uppercase_with_digit
vectors.note: THE v1 drift case. SQLite LIKE is case-insensitive for ASCII, so MCProxy's old NOT LIKE '%:ack%' silently dropped a human message containing ':ACK123' from history sync while the webapp showed it live. GLOB is case-sensitive: the row now stays a normal message everywhere. Firmware only ever emits lowercase ':ack'.

vectors.name: false_positive_feedback
vectors.note: Named directly in predicates.ts's doc-comment as the false positive isAckMessage must NOT match: contains the substring 'ack:' (from 'Feedback:') but never ':ack'.

vectors.name: false_positive_rucksack
vectors.note: Same false-positive shape ('ack:' substring, never ':ack') as called out in predicates.ts's doc-comment.

vectors.name: human_quoting_mid_text
vectors.note: Real production sample: a human quoting an ack mid-sentence still contains a well-formed ':ack765' marker, so it classifies as an ack.

vectors.name: two_ack_markers_first_wins
vectors.note: Both JS RegExp leftmost-match and Python re.search return the FIRST match -- pins match ordering, not just match/no-match.

vectors.name: unicode_digit_rejected
vectors.note: U+0663 ARABIC-INDIC DIGIT THREE. v1 documented a live divergence here (Python \d matched, JS \d did not); v2 pins the ASCII-only answer for every engine: [0-9] in Python and SQLite GLOB, \d in JS (ASCII by definition). Firmware emits ASCII digits only.

vectors.name: space_separator_rejected
vectors.note: The digit must IMMEDIATELY follow ':ack' -- a separator breaks the marker. Pre-v2, webapp messageProcessor.ts's bare .includes(':ack') gate let this human message be consumed as a delivery receipt for a pending message carrying {169 (split(':ack')[1].trim() yields '169'); the digit-anchored gate keeps it a visible chat message.
